question: The current population of a town is 15,250. It increases by 25% and 60% in two successive years but decreases by 57% in the third year. What is the population of the town at the end of the third yea
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the percentage changes into multiplying factors: +25% → 5/4, +60% → 8/5, and −57% → 43/100.

Effective combined multiplier = (5/4) × (8/5) × (43/100) = 86/100 = 0.86

Final population = Initial population × Effective multiplier

Final population = 15250 × 0.86 = 13115

**∴ The correct answer is 13,115.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial population = 15,250

Increase in 1st year = 25%

Increase in 2ⁿd year = 60%

Decrease in 3rd year = 57%

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± R₁/100) × (1 ± R₂/100) × (1 ± R₃/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Final Population = 15250 × (1 + 25/100) × (1 + 60/100) × (1 − 57/100)

⇒ Final Population = 15250 × (125/100) × (160/100) × (43/100)

⇒ Final Population = 15250 × (5/4) × (8/5) × (43/100)

⇒ Final Population = 15250 × (40/20) × (43/100)

⇒ Final Population = 15250 × 2 × (43/100)

⇒ Final Population = 15250 × 86/100

⇒ Final Population = 152.5 × 86

⇒ Final Population = 13,115

**∴ The correct answer is 13,115.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change Formula

If a value changes successively by a% and b%, the effective percentage change is calculated using the formula: Net Change = (a + b + ab/100)%.

Multiplying Factor Method

When a value increases by r%, it becomes (1 + r/100) times the original. For a decrease, it becomes (1 − r/100) times. Multiple successive changes are evaluated by multiplying all these factors directly with the base value.

Fractional Equivalents

Memorising percentage to fraction conversions significantly speeds up calculations. For example, 25% = 1/4 (which gives a multiplier of 5/4 for an increase) and 60% = 3/5 (which gives a multiplier of 8/5 for an increase).
